channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: SushiSwap: Choose a Swap or a Liquidity Pool
item.description: SushiSwap can handle a one-off token trade or a longer-term pool position; the right choice depends on the assets, effort and risks you can take.

item.title: HIFI raises $37 million to expand tokenized markets
item.description: HIFI raised $37 million to extend its stablecoin platform into cards and capital markets, funding tools for firms to settle tokenized assets more easily.

item.title: Blast to wind down after value locked falls more than 98%
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum layer-2 after costs overtook revenue; users can withdraw through its interface until Oct. 26 as value locked sits near $32 million.

item.title: Can a Token Bridge Send Funds to a Different Address?
item.description: A token bridge can send funds to a different destination address when its transfer flow allows it, but that address must work on the receiving chain.

item.title: Four Checks That Can Cut Omnichain Swap Inventory Costs
item.description: Swap providers can reduce inventory costs by forecasting demand, setting reserve limits, comparing full route costs and rebalancing only when the savings justify it.

item.title: Aave V4 Tops $1B in Deposits as Arc and Base Go Live
item.description: Aave says V4 passed $1 billion in deposits in September as Arc and Base went live, adding new lending markets and a way to borrow USDC against tokenized shares.

item.title: How Treasury Teams Reconcile BNB Token Payouts
item.description: Match each BNB payout to its on-chain record, separate transfer amounts from fees, and resolve gaps before closing the treasury ledger.

item.title: What a TRON Confirmation Means
item.description: A TRON confirmation means the block holding a transaction has been solidified by network consensus; learn what that status proves, how to check it and when contract results need a receipt.

item.title: When a Bridge Dashboard Beats a Block Explorer
item.description: A bridge dashboard can connect the source and destination steps faster than an explorer, but only the destination-chain record shows what arrived in your wallet.

item.title: When to Claim a Polygon Withdrawal for Lower Ethereum Gas
item.description: For a Polygon PoS withdrawal, pay the Polygon fee to start, then wait for a quieter Ethereum window to claim; the two steps let you time the larger cost.

item.title: How to Prepare Treasury Funds for Game Item Purchases
item.description: Game studios can prepare treasury funds for item sales by separating operating cash from purchase liquidity and checking token, network and settlement steps before transfers.

item.title: Five Checks Before a Network Delisting Deadline
item.description: Before an exchange stops supporting a network, confirm the deadline, token contract, withdrawal route and test transfer so funds do not land on the wrong chain.

item.title: How to Fund Mantle Marketplace Listing Fees
item.description: A Mantle listing may cost a platform fee, network gas, or both; learn which asset to hold, how to move it onto Mantle, and what to check before signing.

item.title: What to do when a cross-chain transfer fails to arrive
item.description: A failed cross-chain transfer may leave funds committed on the source chain, so check the route status and recovery rules before retrying or claiming a refund.

item.title: Why a liquidity range can leave you with one token
item.description: A concentrated liquidity range can leave your deposit in one token when price moves beyond its bounds. Learn what happens to the position and its fees.

item.title: Blast to wind down Ethereum network as costs top revenue
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum layer-2 network after costs exceeded revenue, with users urged to withdraw by Oct. 26 before the regular interface closes.

item.title: How to Receive Swap XMR in Monero GUI
item.description: A Monero GUI wallet can receive XMR from a swap when you give the service a wallet address, then let the wallet sync and detect the incoming payment.

item.title: What cross-chain signing means for exchange users
item.description: Cross-chain signing can move assets between networks, but the steps differ between exchange accounts and wallets, and each approval has a specific purpose.

item.title: When should wallet traders trust a transaction?
item.description: Wallet traders should set confirmation thresholds by chain and trade size: quick checks suit small moves, while larger transfers need more time to settle.

item.title: How to Estimate Price Impact on a BNB Chain Swap
item.description: Estimate a swap’s price impact by comparing its quoted rate with the pool’s current price, then account for fees, route depth and price movement.
